title: Tennent's (Wellpark Brewery)
notes: 1.5-hour behind-the-scenes tour of Scotland's oldest lager brewery (brewing since 1500s), 18+. Runs 7 days a week. Standard from £17pp; tour + pub meal package from £47pp; accessible tours and private tours (from £300) also bookable on site.

title: BrewDog
notes: 1.5-hour tour of the brewhouse, beer museum and HQ with tastings throughout, 18+. Scheduled Fri–Sun. Active production site (~40 min walking, 5 flights of stairs). 25% discount for Equity Punk shareholders.

title: Belhaven Brewery

title: Stewart Brewing

title: Drygate Brewing Co
notes: ~1-hour guided tour behind the glass of the custom brewery plus a tutored tasting of the core range, 18+. Scheduled Wed 5:30pm & 7:30pm and Sun 1pm/3pm/5pm. Max 12 per slot; wheelchair friendly. (Live tour/booking page confirmed via search; site returned 403 to automated fetch.)

title: Bellfield Brewery
notes: 45-min tour of the brewhouse with a guided tasting of 4 beers (Scotland's leading gluten-free brewery; Scottish Brewery of the Year 2023), 18+. Runs Fri, Sat & Sun. Booked via the brewery's own taproom/events page.

title: Fyne Ales
notes: 40-min family-farm brewery tour, Sat 12:30 & 3:30pm plus Sundays. Standard tour £10 (incl. half pint); Tasting Tour £15 (incl. tasting flight). Booked by email (stewart@fyneales.com) via the site. On-site Brewery Tap and shop open daily.

title: Black Isle Brewery
notes: Free ~30-min tour of the organic farm brewery with a sample of a couple of beers; offered daily approx. 10am–3:30pm. Also runs paid seasonal workshops (garden, harvest, etc.). Shop Mon–Sat.

title: Arran Brewery
location: Brodick, Isle of Arran, North Ayrshire
notes: Guided tour of the brewing process ending with a tasting in the shop; includes an Arran Brewery half-pint glass to take home. Scheduled ~1pm on most weekdays; advance booking required via the site's contact page (min 2 people).

title: Innis & Gunn
location: Edinburgh, City of Edinburgh (also Glasgow taprooms)
notes: ~90-min guided journey through the brewery's history and brewing process with any 6 x 1/3-pint beers of your choice. Available Thu–Sun, advance booking. A tasting/brewery experience rather than a walk-through production tour. (Booking page confirmed via search; automated fetch returned 404.)

title: Tempest Brewing Co
notes: Brewery tour plus a tap session (table in the 16-tap taproom to sample the beers). Runs Saturdays 12–6pm, booked by prior arrangement via tours@tempestbrewco.com. A short walk from Tweedbank rail station.

title: Traquair House Brewery
notes: Notable 18th-century brewery beneath the chapel of Scotland's oldest inhabited house – one of the oldest working breweries in Britain. 30-min guided tour with a tasting of its 3 ales; tour £9pp, tour + tasting ~£25pp. By pre-booking/arrangement (enquiries@traquair.co.uk). House & brewery open Apr–Oct + Nov weekends.

title: The Orkney Brewery

title: Cloudwater Brew Co

notes: Guided brewery tour with tasting at Unit 18, Piccadilly Trading Estate; bookable direct on own site (also sold as gift cards). Check site for scheduled dates.

title: The Runaway Brewery

title: Bowland Brewery

description_md:
From Hive to Pint is Hiver's introduction to what bees and beer have in common. Over 50 minutes in the Bermondsey taproom you'll taste a selection of beer, cider and honey, with snacks, and find out how raw honey goes from the hive into a pint.

Most beer tastings only cover the beer. This one also shows where the honey comes in. Hiver ferments its beers with raw honey, so you'll taste the honeys alongside the drinks and pick out how each one changes the finished beer. It's a relaxed, sociable tasting, and it works well before a wander along the rest of the Beer Mile.

# When it runs

Tastings are held at the taproom from Friday to Sunday (Fridays 4pm–10pm, Saturdays 11am–late and Sundays 12pm–9pm). Check Hiver's booking page for the start times available on your date.

# Who it's for

It's a good choice for first-timers, couples and small groups who want something more interesting than a round at the bar, and anyone curious about bees. Everyone must be 18 or over, and ID may be checked.

# About Hiver

Hiver is a London honey beer brand, born out of an admiration for the city's urban beekeepers and a passion for craft beer. Its beers use only British ingredients and are fermented with raw honey, and the range includes a Honey Blonde Beer and a Honey Brown Ale. Hiver is one of the longest-standing venues on the Bermondsey Beer Mile, and its taproom on Stanworth Street has a live colony of bees in an exhibition hive on the wall.

# Good to know

- Hiver's taproom is on Stanworth Street, Bermondsey, London SE1 3NY, a short walk from London Bridge and Bermondsey stations.
- Hiver's beer contains wheat (gluten), and some food matches contain wheat and lactose and may contain traces of nuts. Let Hiver know about dietary needs in advance at experiences@hiverbeers.com.
- Booking changes can be made up to 2 weeks before your date.

description_md:

The Bermondsey Beer Mile is mostly about beer, but Hiver also has a tasting for cider fans. Hiver's Cider Tasting is a tutored session built around a top-five pick from the UK's cideries, with a host who explains what you're drinking.

The tasting covers cider's history, the main styles you'll come across and how cider is made, from apple to glass. Tasting five ciders side by side makes it much easier to tell dry from sweet and still from sparkling, and to see how different producers approach the same fruit.

# Who it's for

It suits cider drinkers who want to get to know the category better, and mixed groups where not everyone drinks beer. It's also a good fit with the beer tastings if you're visiting with friends who prefer different drinks. Everyone must be 18 or over.

Tastings take place at the taproom Friday to Sunday (Fridays 4pm–10pm, Saturdays 11am–late and Sundays 12pm–9pm). Check Hiver's booking page for available slots.

description_md:
Hiver's Cider Making Workshop is a hands-on 2.5-hour session in its Bermondsey events space. You'll work through the cider-making process yourself, from preparing the apples to pressing them, and you'll go home with bottles of your own cider.

# What you'll do

You'll start by preparing your apples, then press them to extract the juice that becomes cider. Along the way the host explains how the juice turns into cider, and you'll taste ciders and apples so you can see how fruit and method shape the finished drink. There's a cheese and crackers snack plate to keep you going.

# Small groups

The workshop is capped at 12 people, so everyone gets hands-on time at the press and plenty of chances to ask questions. That small size also makes it a good choice for a birthday or a group of friends.

description_md:
Hiver's honey beers start with the hive, and this workshop shows you how honey is harvested. Over 1.5 hours in the Hiver events space in Bermondsey, you'll extract honey yourself with expert guidance, and go home with a jar of the honey you harvested.

# What you'll do

Your host takes you through the harvest step by step, explaining how honey gets from the comb into the jar. Then it's your turn: you'll do the extraction yourself, with help on hand throughout. You'll learn about bees and the honey they make as you go, and you'll see why the honey Hiver uses matters so much to its beers.

# Who it's for

Unlike most Beer Mile experiences, this one is open to anyone aged 14 or over, so it works well for families with teenagers, curious food lovers and anyone thinking about beekeeping. Groups are up to 20 people, which suits a team outing or a celebration with friends. At £35 per person it's also one of the more affordable hands-on experiences in Bermondsey.

# When it runs

Honey harvesting runs from September to March. Check Hiver's booking page for dates.

description_md:
Hiver started out of admiration for London's urban beekeepers, and this experience takes you to meet them. You'll spend two hours at Bee Urban in Kennington Park, close to Kennington and Oval tube stations, learning how bees live and work in the middle of the city, then finish with a tutored tasting of Hiver's honey beers.

# What you'll do

- **Meet the bees.** An expert beekeeper explains how a beehive is organised and how the bee life cycle works.
- **Get hands-on.** You'll be "suited and booted" in a beekeeping suit, then open the hive with the beekeeper, handle a frame and see the colony at work.
- **Learn about urban beekeeping.** You'll find out how bees thrive in London and what it takes to keep them in the city.
- **Taste the results.** You'll finish with a tutored tasting of three of Hiver's award-winning honey beers, with food matching and some nibbles.

On very wet days, when the hives can't be opened safely, the beekeeper builds a hive with the group instead and focuses on hive by-products. So you still get the full experience, whatever the weather.

# When it runs

The beekeeping season runs from April to September, when the bees are most active. Check Hiver's booking page for current dates, including any winter sessions.

# What to wear

Beekeeping suits are provided. Wear closed shoes and socks that cover your ankles. Shorts and skirts are fine under the suit.

Your beekeeper explains how the hive is organised and what the bees are doing at that point in the season. Then you'll open the hive together. You'll handle a frame and see the colony up close. Afterwards, a honey tasting shows how much flavour varies between honeys.
